alt.en: A black and white photograph of a two-storey house with a stone ground floor and clapboard upper floor, shuttered windows and a small canopy over the door, beside a large old tree, with a lawn and garden beds in front.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro de una casa de dos plantas, con la planta baja de piedra y la alta de tablas, ventanas con contraventanas y un pequeño tejadillo sobre la puerta, junto a un gran árbol viejo, con césped y parterres delante.

caption.en: The Shakers' schoolhouse at New Lebanon, New York, built about 1839 and photographed in 1962: New Lebanon was the Shakers' leading village, and Mary Hazzard, whose songbook holds this song, was a sister there.
caption.es: La escuela de los shakers en New Lebanon (Nueva York), construida hacia 1839 y fotografiada en 1962: New Lebanon era la aldea principal de los shakers, y Mary Hazzard, en cuyo cancionero está esta canción, era hermana allí.

source: Historic American Buildings Survey, June 1962, FRONT (WEST) ELEVATION. - Shaker Schoolhouse, Shaker Road, New Lebanon, Columbia County, NY (HABS NY-3259); Jack E. Boucher, photographer
library: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division
licenceEvidence: Item rights advisory: "No known restrictions on images made by the U.S. Government; images copied from other sources may be restricted." (https://www.loc.gov/rr/print/res/114_habs.html). Photographer named in the record: Boucher, Jack E., who "worked for the National Park Service from 1958 to 2006" (https://www.nps.gov/subjects/southfloridacollections/jack-boucher.htm). An original HABS survey photograph, no line crediting another source.
credit: Library of Congress, Prints & Photographs Division, HABS NY,11-NELEB.V,10-3

alt.en: A printed page headed Celestial Choir: a tune written in small letters (c, d, e, g) between bar lines under the words of the first verse, then three more numbered verses.
alt.es: Una página impresa titulada Celestial Choir: una melodía escrita con letras pequeñas (c, d, e, g) entre barras de compás bajo la letra de la primera estrofa, y después tres estrofas numeradas más.

caption.en: Celestial Choir, a Shaker hymn about the dance in the Canterbury Shakers' hymnal of 1852, A Sacred Repository of Anthems and Hymns; its fourth verse sings "To bow and bend be not ashamed, For angels bow low down".
caption.es: Celestial Choir, un himno shaker sobre la danza en el himnario de los shakers de Canterbury de 1852, A Sacred Repository of Anthems and Hymns; su cuarta estrofa canta "To bow and bend be not ashamed, For angels bow low down" (no te avergüences de inclinarte y doblarte, pues los ángeles se inclinan hasta el suelo).

source: A Sacred Repository of Anthems and Hymns, for Devotional Worship and Praise (Canterbury, N.H., 1852), p. 195, "Celestial Choir"
library: Princeton Theological Seminary Library (scan on the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed at Canterbury, N.H., 1852, with no author named in print. US: published before 1931. EU and Israel: an anonymous work's 70 years from publication ended in 1922, and anyone compiling a book in 1852 died long before 1956. Faithful scan of a flat page.
credit: Princeton Theological Seminary Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of close-set text with the running head In the Twelve Christian Virtues, page 297, and numbered paragraphs headed Simplicity and Meekness.
alt.es: Una página impresa de texto apretado con el titulillo In the Twelve Christian Virtues, página 297, y párrafos numerados titulados Simplicity y Meekness.

caption.en: The Shakers' own account of simplicity, one of their twelve Christian virtues, in A Summary View of the Millennial Church (1848): "True gospel simplicity implies a godly sincerity, and a real singleness of heart".
caption.es: La explicación que los propios shakers daban de la sencillez, una de sus doce virtudes cristianas, en A Summary View of the Millennial Church (1848): "True gospel simplicity implies a godly sincerity, and a real singleness of heart" (la verdadera sencillez del evangelio implica una sinceridad piadosa y una auténtica unidad de corazón).

source: Calvin Green and Seth Y. Wells, A Summary View of the Millennial Church, or United Society of Believers, Commonly Called Shakers, second edition (Albany: C. Van Benthuysen, 1848), Part VII, chapter I, p. 297
library: University of Toronto, Robarts Library (scan on the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed at Albany, 1848 (second edition; first edition 1823, by the same two authors). US: published before 1931. EU and Israel: authors already writing in 1823 were born before about 1805 and died long before 1956, so life plus 70 has run out. Faithful scan of a flat page.
credit: University of Toronto, Robarts Library, via the Internet Archive
